question: Which canonical read and snapshot owner can replace repeated traversals or duplicate subscriptions without changing observable state?
trigger: The owner asked for a best-api-review audit of every open ledger unit, frozen from status at fe0e9599a6 on 2026-10-04 (39 units), and judged afresh because earlier verdicts came from a weaker model. It asked for verdicts only, so no plan, build or panel follows in this run. This scope was open as pursue-unbound at queue position 2. It is also the unit next returned.
requirements: Read one coherent document or root at its committed or draft lifetime with installed read capabilities intact.
Answer a consumer's precise dependency (presence, payload, path, selection) from the canonical commit without enumerating unrelated changes or keeping a second change store.
Retain historical snapshot locations; branched accepted and projected history must not corrupt a shared index.
Observers see each published commit once, after publication, with failures routed to the lifecycle error sink.
Plite React publishes mounted selector updates after app commit listeners and before its private source fences, preserving text-sync and decoration ordering.
Public API teaches one way per job; VISION names commit listeners, not a second snapshot-listener vocabulary.
evidenceReuse: Reused the 09-11 membership comparison and the 09-16 branch analysis as design evidence, and the demand-driven plan's production receipts as that plan's own claims. Rechecked on the live tree the commit.ts per-key membership, use-editor-selector demand gating, snapshot-index copy-on-branch and its test, the configuration-scoped read view cache, notifyListeners ordering and argument shapes, every production caller of editor.subscribe and subscribeCommit, private source-phase ordering in the commit fence, and the public docs. Read the June 2026 taste plan that kept the split. No tests, benchmarks or browsers were run.
summary: The job is to read canonical state and observe commits without repeated traversal or duplicate subscriptions. Live source has adopted both prior targets. commit.ts answers per-key path membership from presence plus old-path identity with a per-commit memo, the selector context requests aggregate sets only when matching listener maps exist, and snapshot-index forks provenance when an older shared source branches, with a regression test. Their plan stays blocked only on whole-checkout gates and an unchanged native burst-timing budget, which is proof debt, not design. The fresh deletion test finds the duplicate the question names. BaseEditor exposes subscribe(SnapshotListener) and subscribeCommit(EditorCommitListener). The only caller of notifyListeners always passes a commit, both kinds receive commit and snapshot, the sole production editor.subscribe caller is the Plite provider, and debugging.mdx wrongly says subscribe is needed to get the snapshot. A June 2026 taste round kept the split by intended use (persistence versus replay). That split no longer corresponds to different delivery, so delete public subscribe and SnapshotListener and keep subscribeCommit, with the provider keeping its later phase privately.

callSites.current: editor.subscribe((snapshot, commit) => save(snapshot)) and editor.subscribeCommit((commit, snapshot) => sync(commit)) are both public on BaseEditor; notifyListeners calls commit listeners, then snapshot listeners, for the same commit; the Plite provider uses editor.subscribe.
callSites.proposed: editor.subscribeCommit((commit, snapshot) => save(snapshot)) is the only public subscription (proposed: remove BaseEditor.subscribe and the root SnapshotListener export); the Plite provider keeps its post-commit-listener publication through the private listener-state subscribe phase.

reconciliation.question: Should path-stable snapshot indexes keep mutating one shared provenance record when authored accepted and projected history can branch from the same source snapshot?
reconciliation.reason: Its copy-on-branch target landed in advancePathStableSnapshotIndex with a fork regression test. The remaining reads gap is the duplicate public subscription.

alternatives: Keeping the adopted invalidation and branch-recovery targets as they are is right, but keeping both public subscription methods loses, because they deliver the same per-commit payload.

Deleting public editor.subscribe and SnapshotListener and keeping subscribeCommit is selected. Every commit consumer gets one public subscription, and the Plite provider keeps its existing private post-listener phase.
Deleting subscribeCommit and keeping subscribe is rejected. subscribeCommit has about 28 production callers against one for subscribe, and VISION teaches commit listeners.
Renaming the survivor to editor.subscribe((commit, snapshot)) is a naming choice for best-api. It churns every subscribeCommit caller for no behavior gain.

Moving the provider into the private 'commit' source phase is rejected as the adoption path, because that phase already depends on registration order between the provider decoration source and each view fence.
Replacing the generic selector store (E06) is still unattributed and is not reopened.
Deleting the 'decoration' commit kind as consumer-named is rejected. Docs define it as range-paint impact, and two Plite owners consume it.
proofLimits: Source review only, with no tests, benchmarks or browsers run. The adopted invalidation work keeps its plan's open gates, the strict whole-checkout checks and the www native burst-timing budget (405-455 ms against 373.4 ms, which the plan attributes to paced paint waits without resolving it). The subscription cut's notification-order safety for the Plite provider, Plate stores and history or Yjs listeners is unproven. public-state.ts has another session's uncommitted edits elsewhere in the file, so its lines are cited at HEAD.
